title: AuthN/AuthZ tiering: experimental contract commitments for SSO (SAML) and RBAC
creator: Lila Morgan
description: Problem: Sales and Legal report long cycles negotiating SSO (SAML) and RBAC commitments in enterprise contracts. Engineering needs clear scope to implement per-tier controls (Dedicated vs Private) and Product needs pricing signals and playbook language. This experiment will evaluate a constrained set of contract commitments and packaging options that balance buyer trust with operational cost and risk. Goals: 1) Reduce sales cycle friction by providing a clear, prescriptive set of commitments for SSO (SAML) and RBAC. 2) Measure impact on deal conversion and average ARR for offers that include these commitments. 3) Produce contract language and checklist for Security Questionnaires that sales can attach to RFPs.
acceptance_criteria: Define two canonical packaging tiers for enterprise auth: 'Enterprise+SSO' (SAML, basic RBAC) and 'Enterprise+SSO+RBAC-Advanced' (fine-grained role bindings, audit logs).
Draft contract clauses (security addendum) for each tier and get Legal sign-off.
Engineering provides implementation impact assessment (surface area, ETA, and ongoing support cost) for both tiers.
Pilots with 3 sales opportunities completed and measurable effect on time-to-close recorded.
Updated Security Questionnaire templates and a one-page sales cheat sheet distributed to GTM.
Experiment metrics defined and dashboarded: conversion delta, average ARR uplift, average negotiation days saved, engineering effort (SWE-weeks).
updates: 2025-02-13: Kickoff sync with Sales, Legal, Security, and Eng. Agreed scope: focus on SAML 2.0 SSO + enterprise RBAC (roles, role-binding audit) rather than custom OIDC connectors for experiment MVP.

2025-02-18: Legal provided preliminary addendum draft (see related_links). They requested precise SLAs for account administration actions and clarity on customer vs Redwood responsibilities for IdP configs.

2025-02-21: Engineering (ENG-4123) returned initial impact doc: ~6 SWE-weeks to ship 'SSO baseline' across Hosted/Dedicated; additional ~4 SWE-weeks to implement audit-grade RBAC and admin UI for role management in Private deployments. Identified dependencies on platform RBAC design decisions (see dependencies).
2025-02-25: Sales shared three active opportunities willing to pilot; two mentioned procurement needs a 'contractual acceptance window' for IdP testing and rollback language.

2025-03-01: Security completed threat model for SSO/RBAC commitments. Recommend adding explicit KMS/HSM note for Private customers in contracts and a requirement checkbox in the security questionnaire.

2025-03-04: Product worked with Pricing to produce two offer structures: a) 'SSO Add-on' fee as a one-time onboarding charge plus per-seat admin fee, b) 'Included in Enterprise' higher tier with discounted onboarding. Decided to AB test both approaches in pilot opportunities.

2025-03-05: PM update: preparing legal-ready addendum and sales cheat sheet; onboarding playbook draft to be created with ENG and Solutions by 2025-03-12. Next step: formal pilot kickoff with first customer on 2025-03-10.
comments: Jordan Kim (assignee) 2025-02-20: Engineering flags that Hosted API already supports SSO via proxy routing, but Dedicated/Private require installer and admin UX. Need to scope rollback plan for misconfigured IdPs.

Ravi Patel (Legal) 2025-02-18: Legal prefers narrow, testable commitments (e.g., 'support SAML 2.0' and 'role change audit log retention 90 days') over vague statements. Also recommends customer-owned IdP certificates and clear incident notification obligations.
Marta Ruiz (Sales Ops) 2025-02-25: Sales wants a one-page checklist for procurement that maps features to contract language — important for faster procurement reviews.
Abby Chen (Security) 2025-03-01: For Private deployments, require explicit KMS/HSM integration note and a monthly attestation option for high-risk customers.
decision: Adopt two-tier contractual offering for the experiment: (1) SSO baseline as an add-on or included at higher tier; (2) Advanced RBAC with audit retention and admin UI as a premium tier. Legal to finalize addendum; Eng to deliver scoped MVP for pilot customers. Pricing will A/B test onboarding fee vs included tier uplift.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Engineering underestimates integration complexity for Private deployments. Mitigation: Blocker gating and separate scope for Private-specific installer work; offer pilot customers a managed onboarding option.
Risk: Sales teams overpromise features during negotiation. Mitigation: Clear sales cheat sheet + strict gating to confirm Legal-signed addendum before commit.
Risk: Contract language triggers compliance requests beyond scope. Mitigation: Security questionnaire templates include clear option boxes and examples of supported IdP configurations.
Risk: Pricing reduces deal velocity if add-on perceived as high cost. Mitigation: A/B test including feature vs add-on and track conversion closely.

Prepare retro template to capture negotiation friction points and required clause edits at pilot end (target 2025-03-30).
